topic: How do interference mitigation techniques adapt when handling tunneled versus non-tunneled traffic in multi-beam satellite systems?
consensus_response: Tunneling necessitates sophisticated beamforming and pre-distortion to manage array factors, while non-tunneled traffic relies on robust link budgeting for direct interference mitigation. While both require techniques like rate-splitting and dynamic beam allocation,  non-tunneled traffic benefits from LoS propagation, allowing for more straightforward resource management.
reference_context: Multibeam satellite systems employ diverse techniques to mitigate interference. Tunneling utilizes complex beamforming arrays to manage overlapping beams, while non-tunneled traffic leverages direct line-of-sight propagation and robust link budgeting. Both approaches aim to enhance network performance but require distinct mitigation strategies.
